institutionName: University of North Carolina at Greensboro

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to choose a University with interesting courses within my interest area. I wanted to try some courses that were a bit different from Ethology. Experiencing American campus life was also a significant factor in choosing.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I had a wonderful semester there! The pros of living in a "small" city like Greensboro in the US are you form close bonds with people there, and you have to go on trips to see the US on the weekends and holidays. The campus is really nice, they always have so many events, and nice facilities u can use for free. The Food is alright there (the caf'), but compared to other campuses they have a good reputation. Because it's a small city you quickly develop traditions (fx going to Corner Bar every Tuesday to get 1 dollar beer) and that brings the internationals close together. 
The cons are that is a small city with less to do compared to staying in a big city, and that the academic levels are mixed depending on the professor.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very confusing to me. They had so many requirements that were hard to understand and complete. But they had a really nice lady at their office who would respond to all my "stupid" questions, so it worked out fine in the end.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
They offered to pick us up from the airport if you arrived on a specific day. 
They had sent arrival information before our arrival so we knew where to go.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was good. They had the whole week planned with activities and information. Although it could be nice if they had more on the program the first week in terms of activities.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You could choose whatever housing on campus, but they recommended we stayed at Tower Village with the other internationals. Most internationals did that, including me.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: They had multiple options for meal plans depending on if you wanted flex money to buy food on the campus "restaurants", or eat most of the meals in the cafeteria. The dorms had a small kitchen but you have to buy all the kitchen stuff if you want to cook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You share the kitchen and bathrooms so it's good to sit down with your roommates and talk about cleaning and house rules before it's too late.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was all right. What you would expect for American dorms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was confusing and stressful for me. So many things to do and some of them had to be done in a very specific way.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had a portal where you had to complete their tasks before a specific date.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had a nice lady at their office who would reply to all my questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted, but it was difficult to know what was available in their system. If you are registering late many of them might be filled up. Then you have to wait till you get there and ask the professors if they have room for you in their class. During the first week of class, you can try them out and drop them if you don't like them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for classes as early as possible and try them out when you are there, u can always change classes after the first week. You have to keep in mind that they don't tell you if the classes are overlapping, so you have to check that yourself in terms of making your schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very different depending on the professor. Some were really good and some were not.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very different course levels depending on the course, mostly easy. The multiple-choice exams were somewhat easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar to UCPH with PowerPoint lectures - just listening and taking notes. In one of the courses, we had to do a presentation for the class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- History and Theory of Design I. 
- History of Fashion 
- Film Appreciation
- Global Perspectives on Body, Culture, and Dress.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Global Perspectives on Body, Culture, and Dress, because it's in my interest area. In general, courses/classes with Dr. Trisha Kemerly are good. She is a really talented professor.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A lot of Uber's because public transport is bad.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more expensive than I thought, but it was bad timing because the dollar was so high.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good facilities and free stuff to do. A lot of events on campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a very good gym and sports facilities. They have a free museum close to campus. A lot of social events on campus every week. The bus is free for students so it's easy to go downtown.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to Corner Bar every Tuesday to get a one-dollar beer, go to Limelight on Thursdays, and go to Arizona Petes on Fridays to watch line dance. Go on road trips to hike around North Carolina and you can get a cheap bus ride (Flixbus or greyhound) to the bigger cities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the bigger cities and go on road trips to hike.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat easy. Americans are usually really nice. But the area is a bit rough so you have to take precautions.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take part in the activities and be open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I missed my freedom in terms of transport and feeling safe - I can't just walk everywhere alone.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Americans are very nice, open, and talkative.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy the multiple-choice exams while you can 
Practice small talk and being open like the Americans
Go on trips with friends!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's a social thing to have the full meal plan from the caf.  You see people there all the time so it's a nice place to socialize and meet new people - it is kinda like in the movies.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to experience the US with very nice people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Taking some time to relax.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
